43984-chaucer-for-children-a-golden-key.creator: Unknown
43984-chaucer-for-children-a-golden-key.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Six of the Canterbury Tales are thus presented, in sections of  from 10 to 200 lines, mingled with prose narrative. ‘Chaucer for  Schools’ is issued to meet a widely-expressed want, and is especially  adapted for class instruction. It may be profitably studied in  connection with the maps and illustrations of ‘Chaucer for Children.’_

arxiv-2204-09481.title: Unsupervised Ranking and Aggregation of Label Descriptions for Zero-Shot Classifiers
arxiv-2204-09481.creator: Angelo Basile, Marc Franco-Salvador, Paolo Rosso
arxiv-2204-09481.description: Abstract Zero-shot text classifiers based on label descriptions embed an input text and a set of labels into the same space: measures such as cosine similarity can then be used to select the most similar label description to the input text as the predicted label.

arxiv-2307-11891.title: Advancements in the GravAD Pipeline: Template Reduction and Testing Simulated Signals for Black Hole Detection
arxiv-2307-11891.creator: William E. Doyle
arxiv-2307-11891.description: Abstract This paper introduces significant improvements to the GravAD pipeline, a Python-based system for gravitational wave detection. These advancements include a reduction in waveform templates, implementation of simulated signals, and optimisation techniques. By integrating these advancements, GravAD exhibits increased performance, efficiency, and accuracy in processing gravitational wave data.

arxiv-2309-05052.description: Abstract The formation mechanism of high-concentration dwarf galaxies is still a mystery. We perform a comparative study of the intrinsic shape of nearby low-mass galaxies with different stellar concentration. The intrinsic shape is parameterized by the intermediate-to-major axis ratios B/A and the minor-to-major axis ratios C/A of triaxial ellipsoidal models. Our galaxies ( 10 7.5 ​ M ⊙ 10^{7.

In the trend towards hardware specialization, FPGAs play a dual role as accelerators for offloading, e.g., network virtualization, and as a vehicle for prototyping and exploring hardware designs. While FPGAs offer versatility and performance, integrating them in larger systems remains challenging.

pmc-11417908.title: Abnormal Vestibulo–Ocular Reflex Function Correlates with Balance and Gait Impairment in People with Multiple Sclerosis
pmc-11417908.creator: Marco Tramontano, Laura Casagrande Conti, Amaranta Soledad Orejel Bustos, Nicola Ferri, Tommaso Lelli, Ugo Nocentini, Maria Grazia Grasso, Andrea Turolla, Paolo Pillastrini, Leonardo Manzari
pmc-11417908.description: Background: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is the most prevalent autoimmune neurological condition in the world, leading to a wide variety of symptoms, including balance disorders. Objective: To evaluate the angular vestibulo–ocular reflex (aVOR) of all six semicircular canals (SCCs) through Head Impulse (HIMP) and Suppression HIMP (SHIMP) paradigms and any correlations with clinical balance scales.

pmc-11510519.title: Theoretical Investigation of Rate Coefficients and Dynamical Mechanisms for N + N + N Three-Body Recombination Based on Full-Dimensional Potential Energy Surfaces
pmc-11510519.creator: Chong Xu, Zhenxuan Wei, Huayu Hu, Xixi Hu, Daiqian Xie
pmc-11510519.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Three-body recombination reactions, in which two particles form a bound state while a third one bounces off after the collision, play significant roles in many fields, such as cold and ultracold chemistry, astrochemistry, atmospheric physics, and plasma physics. In this work, the dynamics of the recombination reaction for the N3 system over a wide temperature range (5000–20,000 K) are investigated in detail using the quasi-classical trajectory (QCT) method based on recently developed full-dimensional potential energy surfaces.

pmc-11652574.title: Gaze-action coupling, gaze-gesture coupling, and exogenous attraction of gaze in dyadic interactions
pmc-11652574.creator: Roy S Hessels, Peitong Li, Sofia Balali, Martin K Teunisse, Ronald Poppe, Diederick C Niehorster, Marcus Nyström, Jeroen S Benjamins, Atsushi Senju, Albert A Salah, Ignace T C Hooge
pmc-11652574.description: In human interactions, gaze may be used to acquire information for goal-directed actions, to acquire information related to the interacting partner’s actions, and in the context of multimodal communication. At present, there are no models of gaze behavior in the context of vision that adequately incorporate these three components.

pmc-12371010.title: Glucosylsphingosine affects mitochondrial function in a neuronal cell model
pmc-12371010.creator: Valeria Nikolaenko, Reddy Vootukuri, Simon Eaton, Jenny Hällqvist, Tomas Baldwin, Kevin Mills, Wendy Heywood
pmc-12371010.description: Gaucher disease arises from mutations in glucocerebrosidase resulting in accumulation of glucosylceramide, which is deacylated to glucosylsphingosine. Mutations in glucocerebrosidase are the greatest known genetic risk factor for Parkinson’s disease. Glucosylsphingosine is a biomarker for Gaucher disease and studies demonstrate its relevance to disease pathology, yet the mechanisms of its toxicity remain little understood.

pmc-12551249.title: Nonlinear association between serum iron levels and moderate-to-severe uremic pruritus in peritoneal dialysis patients: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12551249.creator: Wenjie Yu, Jing He, Zhiyao Bao, Zhaoting Li, Chunyan Zhang, Jingyuan Xie, Hong Ren, Xiaomin Huang, Tian Xu
pmc-12551249.description: PurposeTo evaluate the occurrence of uremic pruritus among peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients and explore its correlation with serum iron levels.MethodsA cross-sectional study was carried out on 189 PD patients at a single center in China. The severity of pruritus was assessed through the validated 5-D Itch Scale questionnaire.

pmc-12559393.title: Triglyceride-glucose index variability and risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality
pmc-12559393.creator: Jimin Park, Duk Ho Kim, Jun-Hyuk Lee
pmc-12559393.description: Triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a reliable marker of insulin resistance with predictive value for cardiovascular risk. While metabolic variability independently impacts cardiovascular outcomes and mortality, the clinical significance of TyG index variability remains unclear. We investigated whether higher TyG index variability increases the risk of mortality.

pmc-12662008.title: Rare but not forgotten: Therapeutic advancements for rare childhood cancers
pmc-12662008.creator: Jacquelyn N. Crane, Urania Dagalakis, Robyn D. Gartrell, Kris Ann P. Schultz, Theodore W. Laetsch
pmc-12662008.description: Cancers in children represent less than 1% of all new cases of cancer. While all cancers are rare during childhood, certain types are particularly rare. Multi-institutional pediatric trials and coordinated efforts between pediatric and adult groups have resulted in recent key advances in the treatment of certain rare pediatric cancers.

pmc-12742724.title: Exploring leprosy perceptions in South Sulawesi, Indonesia: A mixed-methods study on knowledge, attitudes, practices, and stigma
pmc-12742724.creator: Ralalicia Limato, Ida A. Sutrisni, Rahmat Sagara, Asyhad F. Abdillah, Yuliati Yuliati, Al Kadri, Sri V. Muchtar, Iqbal Elyazar, Hardyanto Soebono, Jennifer I. Van Nuil, Marlous L. Grijsen, Jessica Fairley, Julia Robinson
pmc-12742724.description: Leprosy-related stigma has a profound impact on affected individuals and their communities. Embedded within the MetLep trial of adjunctive metformin for multibacillary leprosy, we explored knowledge and perceptions of leprosy in endemic communities in Sulawesi, Indonesia. We conducted a mixed-methods cross-sectional study using interview-administered questionnaires and qualitative methods.

pmc-12843407.title: Influence of Suillus grevillea on the Root Morphology, Growth and Rhizosphere Soil Properties of Quercus variabilis Blume Seedlings with Root Pruning
pmc-12843407.creator: Jinhua Sun, Shu Zhao, Liu Yang, Yazhen Liang, Xitian Yang, Lianfeng Shen, Erhui Guo, Qingxin Li, Yishuo Jia, Lin Zhang, Haoran Liu, Ruiling Sun
pmc-12843407.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Root pruning affects the ability of roots of Quercus variabilis Blume to absorb water and nutrients. Suillus grevillea can form a mutualistic symbiosis with Quercus variabilis Blume. A pot experiment in three compartments with two inoculation treatments (inoculation with Suillus grevillea and noninoculation control) and four different root pruning treatments (0, 1/4, 1/3, and 1/2 of the main root length pruned) was conducted.

pmc-13148282.title: Pharmacist-Led Deprescribing Interventions in Older Adults: A Systematic Review of Medication Appropriateness, Patient Safety, and Clinical Outcomes
pmc-13148282.creator: Esteban Zavaleta-Monestel, Jeaustin Mora-Jiménez, Luis Herrera-Jiménez, Andrea Chaves-Arroyo, Kevin Cruz Mora, Sebastián Arguedas-Chacón
pmc-13148282.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Polypharmacy in older adults is associated with medication-related harm, including adverse drug events, drug-drug interactions, inappropriate prescribing, and hospitalization-related outcomes. This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness and safety of pharmacist-led deprescribing interventions in adults aged ≥65 years. The review was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, and searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Scopus for studies published from January 2020 to December 2024.

pmc-13213979.title: Molecular de-extinction looks to the past to find the molecules of the future
pmc-13213979.creator: David Adam
pmc-13213979.description: t animals for a reservoir of biochemical novelty. Researchers resurrected a molecule from the woolly mammoth via a digital analysis of mammoth DNA. It’s part of a hunt for new antibiotics. Image credit: Shutterstock/Orla. The technique is called molecular de-extinction. The researchers involved are looking to reconstruct the lost species’ individual proteins and smaller protein-like molecules called peptides.

pmc-13335864.title: Strain‐Preserving Transfer of Freestanding Oxide Membranes for Tunable Magnetic Anisotropy
pmc-13335864.creator: Jinfeng Zhang, Yuyue Zhao, Shouzhe Dong, Jingdi Lu, Qing Wang, Fang Xu, Ao Wang, Kunjie Dai, Yueming Huang, Zhengguo Liang, Qiming Lv, Houbing Huang, Wenbin Wu, Lingfei Wang
pmc-13335864.description: Epitaxial strain has been widely used as an effective approach for harnessing magnetic anisotropy (MA) of complex oxide‐based heterostructures, which enables essential building blocks for advanced spintronic applications. However, extending this strain engineering of MA to flexible magnetic systems and devices is largely hindered by strain relaxation during the exfoliation and transfer procedures of freestanding oxide membranes.

pmc-13378373.title: Gut commensal bifidobacteria are associated with restrained inflammatory reprogramming in human monocyte-derived dendritic cells
pmc-13378373.creator: Sayaka Ishihara, Tatsuki Nishimura, Riko Mishima, Eri Mitsuyama, Akira Sen, Hiroki Kaneko, Yukihiro Hishida, Miyuki Tanaka, Toshitaka Odamaki
pmc-13378373.description: SummaryThe gut commensal microbiota helps calibrate systemic innate immunity in humans. Here, we investigated whether gut bifidobacteria are associated with altered inflammatory responsiveness in human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDCs) from healthy adults. Higher abundance of gut-resident Bifidobacterium correlated with lower moDC inflammatory responses to multiple bacterial stimuli.

pmc-13391273.title: The paracrine effects of tumor-resident mesenchymal stem/stromal cells in the microenvironment of brain metastases
pmc-13391273.creator: Tamer Ayberk Kaya, Klaus-Peter Stein, Belal Neyazi, Ali Rashidi, Ulf Dietrich Kahlert, Christian Mawrin, Ibrahim Erol Sandalcioglu, Claudia Alexandra Dumitru
pmc-13391273.description: BackgroundTumor-resident mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) were identified in several cancers, and were implicated in regulating multiple aspects of tumor progression. However, the role of tumor-resident MSCs in the pathophysiology of brain metastases (BrMs) -the most prevalent type of malignant brain tumor- is currently unknown, and was investigated in this study.

pmc-13404209.title: Influence of the Salmonella Infantis pESI plasmid on disinfectant efficacy when in biofilm
pmc-13404209.creator: Emma Davies, Victoria Drauch, Mohammad Alitabar, Darya Fesina, Ludwig Großpointner, Claudia Hess, Francesca Martelli

pmc-13475814.title: A potential stormwater management intervention: Compost incorporation improves infiltration rate and associated soil hydro-physical properties
pmc-13475814.creator: Md Mahfuz Islam, Richard A. McLaughlin, Joshua L. Heitman
pmc-13475814.description: Urbanization associated construction operations, while necessary for infrastructure development, can result in highly disturbed and intentionally, or inadvertently, compacted soils. Compost incorporation into these disturbed soils is a relatively simple intervention that may alleviate compaction and increase important post-construction soil physical properties such as water infiltration capacity.

pmc-13531703.title: How conditions within immigration removal centres in the United Kingdom affect the mental wellbeing of detainees: a scoping review
pmc-13531703.creator: Niamh Gallagher, Tristan Price, Matthew Griggs
pmc-13531703.description: BackgroundImmigration Removal Centres (IRCs) are used to detain people for immigration control by the UK government. This scoping review aims to examine the experiences of detainees within UK IRCs, specifically how conditions within them, including the regime, affect their mental wellbeing.MethodsThe Joanna Briggs Institute guideline for scoping reviews was followed.

pmc-13622904.title: Erosion Potential of Commercial Fluoride‐Free Mouthwashes on Dental Hard Tissues
pmc-13622904.creator: Astrid C Valdivia‐Tapia, Adam B Kelly, Anderson T Hara, Jaime Aparecido Cury, Antonio Pedro Ricomini‐Filho, Frank Lippert
pmc-13622904.description: PurposeMouthwashes often present acidic pH, which raises concerns about their potential contribution to erosive tooth wear. This study evaluated the erosive potential of commercial fluoride‐free mouthwashes using a screening method.MethodsA convenience sample of 81 different mouthwashes was evaluated for their erosion potential (International Organization for Standardization, ISO/FDIS 28888:2013).
